key_insight: ANTAP routes tasks by empirically testing agent capabilities and then using a non-textual geometric projection, making metadata-based manipulation much harder.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more secure and robust orchestration layer for multi-agent systems where routing quality and prompt/description attacks directly affect reliability.
method: Actively query agents to measure real task performance instead of trusting self-descriptions.
Distill these measurements into fixed behavioral operators in a shared semantic space.
Perform routing with a purely non-textual algebraic projection to block description-based attacks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-zero attack success rate against description-based injection attacks, versus 67.3% and above for the description-based router baseline, and a 20% reduction versus the embedding-based baseline under adaptive embedding attacks.
watch_item: Because ANTAP depends on active capability testing, deployment may add latency and require careful test design to avoid incomplete coverage of an agent’s true behavior.
paper_title: Linguistic Firewall: Geometry as Defense in Multi-Agent Systems Routing
